title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
excerpt: AI agents are playing an increasingly important role in physics research. However, existing physics benchmarks only evaluate fixed questions, isolated sub-tasks, or paper reproduction with given solutions, and rarely check research quality alongside correctness. We introduce FrontierPhysics, an end-to-end benchmark with 56 tasks made by 42 physicists based on their own research, covering nine domains across theoretical, computational, and experimental physics. Each task requires agents to review the literature, develop a research plan, conduct research and experiments, and produce structured outputs and scientific manuscripts. Combining deterministic verifiers with expert-authored rubrics…

ai.summary: FrontierPhysics presents a benchmark of 56 end‑to‑end physics research tasks across nine domains, created by 42 physicists, to evaluate AI agents on real research problems.
ai.why: It gives developers a comprehensive suite to test and improve agents that assist or automate physics research.

title: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation
excerpt: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) extends on-policy distillation (OPD) to consolidate capabilities from multiple teachers. Although prior work reports near-perfect in-distribution (IND) distillation performance, we find that this can mask incomplete capability consolidation beyond the supervised distribution. A preliminary study on synthetic reasoning shows that OPD does not fully transfer teachers' generalization capabilities. We then extend this investigation to real-world tasks, evaluating extrapolative and compositional generalization across mathematical reasoning, coding, agent, and long-context capabilities using Qwen3 models. Across extrapolative settings, OPD and MOPD…

ai.summary: A new paper demonstrates that multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) often fails to transfer generalization capabilities from teacher models to students, despite achieving near-perfect in-distribution performance. The authors show through synthetic and real-world tasks that this method masks incomplete capability consolidation outside the supervised distribution.
ai.why: Critical for developers using distillation to compress models, as it highlights a significant risk of degraded out-of-distribution performance that standard metrics might miss.

title: TAC-CoT: Tool-Empowered Implicit Chain-of-Thought via Interleaving Explicit Tokens
excerpt: LLM-based agentic systems are increasingly combined with CoT reasoning to solve tasks that require accurate reasoning, external knowledge, and multi-step deliberation. Yet, explicit CoT incurs substantial generation overhead, while implicit CoT, which replaces textual rationales with compact continuous tokens, does not naturally support the explicit communication interface required for agentic tool-use. We propose TAC-CoT, a tool-empowered adaptive implicit CoT framework that replaces explicit reasoning traces with compact latent reasoning segments while retaining textual tokens only for tool calls, observations, and final answers. This interleaved design enables agentic tool-use without…

ai.summary: TAC‑CoT introduces a tool‑empowered implicit chain‑of‑thought framework that interleaves explicit tokens with compact continuous tokens to enable efficient reasoning in LLM‑based agents.
ai.why: It can reduce generation overhead while preserving tool‑use communication, useful for building efficient agentic systems.

title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
excerpt: Vision-language-action models are typically built on a simple premise: perception is first compressed by visual encoders, and action reasoning begins only afterwards. Yet manipulation often hinges on precisely the visual signals most vulnerable to this abstraction, e.g., local geometry, boundaries, depth, and subtle state changes. This raises a fundamental question: should action policies inherit a fixed visual endpoint, or directly access evolving visual computation? We introduce NEO-VLA, a structurally encoder-free vision-language-action framework. Images are tokenized by lightweight patch convolutional layers and evolve jointly with language throughout the backbone, allowing a…

ai.summary: The NEO‑VLA paper proposes Vision‑Language‑Action policies that access evolving visual computation directly instead of using a fixed visual encoder.
ai.why: This architecture may enable more precise manipulation tasks by preserving fine‑grained visual details for action reasoning.

title: Solv3R: 3D Looped Transformer as a Multi-view Solver
excerpt: Classical structure-from-motion reconstruction proceeds iteratively, refining camera poses and scene geometry from a current estimate. This allows maps to easily expand without recomputing already computed views, or geometry estimates to improve as more observations are provided. Most geometric foundation models, however, predict entire geometry in a single forward pass or update a recurrent state as frames arrive sequentially, making this expansion and refinement non-trivial. We introduce Solv3R, a looped transformer that learns to continue solving multi-view geometry from its current state. Importantly, its update operator is independent of the iteration count, allowing previously refined…

ai.summary: Solv3R introduces a 3D looped transformer that solves multi-view structure‑from‑motion by iteratively refining camera poses and scene geometry, enabling expansion and refinement without recomputing earlier views.
ai.why: It offers a more flexible way to build and update 3D maps, useful for developers of SLAM and AR systems.

title: D3D: Decoupled Diffusion Drafting for Asynchronous Speculative Decoding
excerpt: Target-conditioned diffusion drafters predict candidate tokens in parallel, yet each new block must wait for updated target-model hidden states. This forces drafting and verification to run sequentially, limiting speedup even though each block is generated in one pass. We introduce D3D, a standalone diffusion drafter that removes this inter-round dependency. D3D combines blockwise denoising with auxiliary autoregressive supervision to achieve long accepted prefixes without target hidden states. This independence lets D3D draft successor blocks during verification in one packed pass, enabling asynchronous speculative decoding. We progressively prune layers according to their effect on…

ai.summary: D3D is a standalone diffusion drafter for speculative decoding that removes inter-round dependencies by combining blockwise denoising with auxiliary autoregressive supervision, allowing for longer accepted prefixes without waiting for target-model hidden states.
ai.why: Improves inference speed for LLMs by enabling asynchronous speculative decoding, which is useful for optimizing serving latency.

title: StreamDuo: A Live Commentator and a Research Agent for Unseen Games
excerpt: Streaming video LLMs can now commentate live gameplay, but they are trained and tested on the same games. We study cross-game streaming commentary, in which a model trained on one game commentates games it has never seen, and find that current commentators transfer their timing but not their knowledge of the game world. We propose StreamDuo, which pairs a trainable commentator with a frozen research agent that reads the wiki of the game being played. When the commentator sees something it cannot name, it sends the current frames, and the research agent returns a few wiki entries two seconds later while the stream continues. We train only the commentator, on a single game, in two stages…

ai.summary: StreamDuo pairs a trainable live‑commentary LLM with a frozen research agent that reads a game's wiki, enabling commentary on unseen games by consulting external knowledge when needed.
ai.why: Allows developers to build streaming commentaries that generalize to new games without retraining on each title.

title: Hybrid Computer Use: A Unified Programmatic, Semantic, and Visual Interface for General Agents
excerpt: Computer-use agents increasingly tackle tasks ranging from everyday desktop activities to long-horizon professional workflows. Yet interfaces centered on screenshots and mouse-and-keyboard actions can impose a human-interaction prior, requiring repeated screen interpretation while leaving the computer's semantic and programmatic capabilities underexposed. We argue for exposing these capabilities and letting models choose and combine them. We introduce Hybrid Computer Use (HCU), a unified interface for general agents that combines three complementary channels: programmatic interaction through code and command-line tools, semantic interaction through accessibility (AX), and visual interaction…

ai.summary: The paper introduces Hybrid Computer Use (HCU), a unified interface that lets AI agents combine programmatic, semantic, and visual interactions with a computer instead of relying solely on screenshots and mouse‑keyboard actions.
ai.why: HCU could enable more capable and efficient AI agents for complex desktop and workflow automation tasks.

Given a query vector, MIPS systems search within a database of millions of candidate key vectors for the one that best matches the query. The original data point associated with that best-matching key is then used to handle the query: in RAG, the document that is best suited to answer the question is typically prefixed to the query.
As the number of keys grows to millions and vector dimensions reach thousands, the computational cost of running an exhaustive…

title: Human-to-Robot Transfer via Bridging Representation and Action Space in VLAs
excerpt: Pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies provide a strong starting point for deployment, but adapting them to a target robot and environment still requires costly embodiment-specific demonstrations. Human demonstrations are far easier to collect, yet directly leveraging them is challenging due to the substantial human-robot embodiment gap, particularly when the underlying VLA has been pretrained primarily on robot data. We introduce H2RB (Human-To-Robot Bridge), a human-robot co-training framework for adapting pretrained VLA policies from unpaired human and robot demonstrations. H2RB bridges the embodiment gap at both interfaces: geometry-anchored alignment grounds human and robot…

ai.summary: H2RB (Human‑To‑Robot Bridge) co‑trains vision‑language‑action policies with human demonstrations to bridge the embodiment gap between humans and robots, reducing the need for robot‑specific data.
ai.why: Enables developers to leverage cheap human data to adapt pretrained VLA models to new robots and environments.

title: GameVerse: A Minute-Scale Gameplay Dataset for Long-Horizon Interactive World Modeling
excerpt: Recent advances in interactive world models have made it possible to generate controllable, dynamic environments from action inputs. Yet current models struggle to maintain coherence beyond roughly one minute of rollout, a limitation rooted not in model capacity but in the scarcity of long-horizon training data. Existing gameplay video datasets typically consist of clips under ten seconds, with captions that describe whole clips in coarse and undifferentiated text, which is insufficient for controllable long-horizon generation. We address this with GameVerse, a minute-scale gameplay video dataset purpose-built for long-horizon interactive world modeling. GameVerse contains 69.7K clips…

ai.summary: The GameVerse paper introduces a minute‑scale gameplay dataset containing long‑horizon interaction traces to train world models beyond the typical ten‑second clips.
ai.why: Developers can use the dataset to train models that maintain coherence over longer rollouts, improving interactive AI agents.

title: EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL
excerpt: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has advanced generative model post-training in verifiable domains such as code and mathematics, but evaluating video quality, especially emotional expression, often depends on subjective aesthetics and has no uniquely correct target. Existing approaches typically rely on fixed rewards for visual quality, motion quality, and text alignment that poorly capture emotional intent and can invite reward hacking, while RLHF is difficult to scale and subject to individual aesthetic differences that complicate the calibration of facial, body motion, and chromatic cues across narrative contexts. We introduce EmoReward, a new self-evolving training mechanism…

ai.summary: EmoReward introduces a self‑evolving reward system that calibrates emotional video generation using Group Relative Policy Optimization to avoid fixed‑reward hacking.
ai.why: Provides a framework for developers to train video generators that better capture intended emotional content.

title: SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding
excerpt: Speculative decoding (SD) accelerates large language model inference by reducing the sequential cost of token-by-token generation. Advanced SD methods reduce proposal cost with parallel drafters that predict entire blocks in one forward pass, but overall speedup still depends on acceptance length. On-policy distillation (OPD) can push well-trained drafters beyond acceptance-length plateaus, yet conventional pipelines collect supervision through sequential draft-and-verify rollouts. Our key insight is that on-policy supervision need not inherit these dependencies: a draft block can be supervised using only its reference prefix and draft-sampled history. We propose SpecOPD, a branch-parallel…

ai.summary: SpecOPD introduces branch‑parallel on‑policy distillation for speculative decoding, improving draft acceptance length by training drafters with parallel rollouts rather than sequential draft‑and‑verify.
ai.why: Boosts inference speed of large language models by making speculative decoding more efficient, beneficial for real‑time applications.

title: VA-TDM: A Unified View for Improving Few-Step Diffusion Models by Velocity Adversarial Distillation
excerpt: Few-step distillation offers efficient generation with diffusion and flow models, but preserving quality with only a few sampling steps remains challenging. Distribution-matching methods via score distillation provide a strong foundation, yet they rely on accurately tracking the student's changing distribution. At intermediate generation steps in few-step sampling, student-score estimation can be difficult, and commonly used estimators may describe a different distribution from the one used to update the student. Flow matching allows a more flexible approach to supervision through velocity fields constructed from the student's sampling process. Building on this perspective, we introduce…

ai.summary: VA‑TDM presents Velocity Adversarial Distillation, a method that improves few‑step diffusion model generation by matching student and teacher distributions via a velocity‑based adversarial loss.
ai.why: Helps developers obtain high‑quality images with far fewer diffusion steps, reducing inference cost.

title: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data
excerpt: Teleoperation remains the default way to collect robot demonstrations, but every episode costs robot and operator time, and every new task starts from scratch. We ask whether a coding agent can take over the teleoperator's job. In our DataFarm, the agent receives a data request and one calibration episode of the robot in the target scene and rebuilds the task in simulation: it writes the scene, an expert controller, and a success judge. The simulator supplies exact actions, and a video model conditioned on real images renders each rollout as photographic video, generating all camera views together consistently. The output is real-ready data: synchronized camera views labelled with the…

ai.summary: PyRUA‑DataFarm demonstrates an LLM‑based teleoperator that, given a single calibration episode, generates simulation code, an expert controller, and a success judge to collect robot data cost‑effectively.
ai.why: Developers can deploy the agent to automate data collection for new robot tasks, reducing manual teleoperation effort.

title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?
excerpt: While multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning (RL) excels on long-horizon tasks, its performance gains remain highly sensitive to interaction constraints. Evaluating across sampling breadth K and interaction depth T via Pass@(K,T), we show that trajectory-level RL advantages depend on sufficient turn budgets, diminishing significantly when budgets tighten. Besides, agentic RL does not uniformly elevate single-step decision quality; rather, its strength concentrates in error recovery and long-horizon resilience. To mitigate the deployment risks caused by this budget dependence, we provide a preliminary discussion on the benefits and limitations of process supervision signals and introduce…

title: MUON-RT Reusing the Teacher's Trajectory for Momentum-Free Muon for LLM Self-Distillation
excerpt: Self-distillation methods for large language models with an exponential moving average (EMA) teacher already retain a history of student updates. Muon nevertheless stores a separate momentum buffer, increasing persistent training memory. We propose Muon with Reused Teacher (Muon-RT), which reuses the teacher-student displacement to eliminate momentum buffers for hidden weight matrices. We show that this displacement encodes an exponentially weighted history of applied updates and smooths temporally uncorrelated noise under a local model. ai.summary: Muon‑RT eliminates the momentum buffer in Muon self‑distillation for LLMs by reusing the teacher‑student displacement, achieving memory‑efficient training while preserving update history smoothing.
ai.why: Reduces GPU memory usage for large‑scale LLM self‑distillation, making it more accessible for developers with limited resources.

title: Halley: A Predictive Control Plane for Optical AI Data Center Networks
excerpt: A frontier AI model is trained in an AI data center, on tens of thousands of accelerators joined by a dedicated network, and every training step ends with all of them exchanging data at once. Between racks, that network is optical, and each of its four layers, from lasers to switches, runs a fixed or after-the-fact policy. Lasers sharing an enclosure, cooling, and power can fail together. At a fixed spare ratio, correlated failure provably caps a pool's availability however large it grows. In this paper, we present a comprehensive predictive control plane framework, called Halley, that reads each resource's next state and acts before the failure occurs. ai.summary: Halley proposes a predictive control plane for optical AI data center networks, modeling how laser, cooling, and power failures can limit availability even with high spare ratios.

excerpt: Streaming video understanding requires models to repeatedly decide whether to respond or continue observing. We propose TurnWise, a turn-level GRPO framework that aligns learning with individual streaming decisions. excerpt: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can now process hour-long videos, making extended multi-turn dialogue over a single video a natural mode of use. title: VidDub: Replacement-Aware Distillation for Two-Step Video Dubbing

title: codex 0.167.0
excerpt:
New Features
Open the agent command center with codex agents --no-daemon . The command center and session picker now mark unread results ( #58238 , #58239 , #58263 , #58264 ).
Switch between connected backends from the terminal session picker and keep your drafts when switching ( #58280 , #58457 ).
Preview local image attachments while composing on supported terminals, and open viewed local images from clickable transcript paths ( #58261 , #58446 ).
Find API key and cloud provider options under “Sign in another way.” Enable gcp_setup_wizard to set up Google Cloud Vertex AI with Application Default Credentials or a credential file ( #57857 , #58427 ).
Opt into macOS or Windows system proxy…

ai.summary: OpenAI released version 0.167.0 of the Codex CLI, a command-line interface for interacting with their coding models.
ai.why: Developers using the Codex CLI should update to access the latest features and bug fixes in this incremental release.
